summary: This page presents Keppel REIT's Key Highlights with a focus on its audited Portfolio Statement showing 96.7% committed occupancy and robust rental reversion of +11.5%, alongside financial highlights detailing a distribution to unitholders of \$212.4m per unit and aggregate leverage at 47.9%. All figures are reported in SGD, specifically noting the distribution amount as \$212.4m (not S$ million) and lease expiry data by attributable committed gross rent.

This page presents Keppel REIT's audited portfolio statement, highlighting a total valuation of approximately $11.7 billion across 14 properties and over 5 million square feet of net lettable area as at 31 December 2025. The report details the trade mix by region with Singapore comprising 79.8%, Australia 17.2%, South Korea 2.3%, and Japan 0.7% of the portfolio, alongside green certifications and specific property listings for each location.

This page presents the Financial Highlights for Keppel REIT's annual report, featuring a main table detailing 2025 and 2024 results including property income, net property income, share of associates' results, borrowing costs, and distribution to Unitholders in SGD'000. The content also includes a Balance Sheet summary with total assets, liabilities, and unitholders' funds, alongside a Financial Ratios table showing Distribution per Unit (DPU), yield, interest coverage, and aggregate leverage, all reported in SGD'000.

This page presents the Half-Yearly Results financial table for SGX REIT, reporting distribution to unitholders and property income in SGD'000 alongside borrowing costs. Key figures include Full Year 2025 Distribution of $212,406, Property Income of $274,478, Net Property Income of $215,905, and Borrowing Costs of $(90,354).

This page presents a timeline diagram detailing Keppel REIT's portfolio evolution from 2006 to December 2025, highlighting acquisitions, divestitures, and stake increases across Singapore, Australia, South Korea, and Japan resulting in a \$11.7 billion portfolio value of 14 assets. The text also outlines capital management metrics including aggregate leverage at 47.9% as at 31 December 2025, sustainability financing progress with 79% of borrowings being sustainability-focused, and strategic milestones such as the Net Zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions target by 2050.

This page presents the Board Composition Dashboard for Keppel REIT, detailing tenure distribution (1 director <3 years, 1 director 3-6 years, 3 directors >6 years), gender diversity (2 Female, 4 Male), independence (4 Independent Directors, 2 Non-Independent Directors), age profile (4 directors 60-69 years, 2 directors 70-79 years), and an attendance table tracking meetings attended by each director across the Board, Audit and Risk Committee, Nominating and Remuneration Committee, Environmental, Social and Governance Committee, and Unitholders' Meeting.

This page presents an independent market review of Singapore's economy and office sector, featuring a main table detailing the 2026-2028 islandwide office supply pipeline by project, developer, market location, and estimated net lettable area (NLA) in square feet. The text outlines GDP growth trends across key sectors, existing stock levels by submarket, completed supply, withdrawal volumes, and future supply projections sourced from CBRE.
This page contains the "SINGAPORE ISLANDWIDE FUTURE OFFICE SUPPLY (2026-2028)" table reporting Net Lettable Area in million sf by submarket.

This page presents an Independent Market Review for Singapore, featuring a main table and chart detailing Net Lettable Area, vacancy rates (including Grade A sub-segment), and rental values (Grade A/B with premiums) for the CBD Core from 1Q 2021 to 4Q 2025. The reporting unit is SGD'000 for valuation context where applicable, but the primary data tables use $ psf/month for rents and million sf for area metrics without explicit financial statement schemas such as audited portfolio statements or total return tables.

This page presents an Independent Market Review of Singapore CBD Core (Grade A) Office, featuring two tables tracking Capital Value ($ psf) and Net Yield (%) from 1Q 2021 to 4Q 25 with data sourced from CBRE. The content also includes photographic descriptions of the Keppel Bay Tower in HarbourFront and discusses market developments such as Labrador Tower's completion and the Greater Southern Waterfront project.

This page presents market analysis for the Sydney CBD and Macquarie Park office sectors, featuring two primary data artifacts: a table detailing Sydney CBD demand and supply metrics ('000 sm) from 2021 to 2028, and a table tracking Sydney CBD rent and vacancy trends (A$ psm/year and %) from 4Q 2021 to 4Q 2025. The content outlines investment activity, rental growth projections, yield forecasts, and specific market conditions for both precincts without including audited portfolio statements, total return figures, tenant mix tables, or financial highlights.

This page presents the Independent Market Review for Australia, featuring a Macquarie Park Demand and Supply table tracking Net Absorption, Net New Supply, and Forecasted Net New Supply from 2021 to 2028 in '000 sm, alongside a Rent and Vacancy table reporting Prime Gross Effective Rent (A$ psm/year) and Prime Grade Vacancy (%) for 4Q 2021 through 4Q 2025. The text further details North Sydney market dynamics including net absorption figures, vacancy trends, and rent forecasts, but contains no audited portfolio statements, financial statements, revenue/expense notes, top-ten tenant tables, DPU data, or manager/trustee information.

This page contains market outlook tables and charts for Melbourne CBD and North Sydney office demand, supply, rent, and vacancy rates reported in Australian dollars ($A) and thousands of square meters ('000 sm). The primary artifacts include a table forecasting Net Absorption, Net New Supply, and Forecasted Net New Supply for North Sydney from 2021 to 2028, alongside data on Prime Gross Effective Rent and Prime Grade Vacancy from 4Q 2021 to 4Q 2025.

This page features the **PERTH CBD RENT AND VACANCY** table detailing prime gross effective rents and vacancy rates from 4Q 2021 to 4Q 2025, alongside a **PERTH CBD DEMAND AND SUPPLY ('000 sm)** table forecasting net absorption and new supply through 2028.

The page presents the "SEOUL CBD DEMAND AND SUPPLY ('000 pyeong)" table and charts detailing net absorption, new supply, and forecasted construction volumes from 2021 to 2028. It further includes the "SEOUL GRADE A NEW CONSTRUCTION ('000 pyeong)" table breaking down supply by submarket (CBD, YBD, GBD) and the "SEOUL CBD RENT AND VACANCY" table tracking Grade A net effective rent in KRW per pyeong/month and vacancy rates from 4Q 2021 to 4Q 2025.

The page presents the Property Portfolio Statistics table for Keppel REIT as at 31 December 2025, reporting a net lettable area of 5,493,917 sf (510,397 sm), total valuation of \$11.7 billion, and committed occupancy of 96.7% based on SGD'000 or equivalent reporting units.

This page features the **Asset Distribution by Value (%)** and **Asset Distribution by NLA (%)** tables for Keppel REIT as at 31 December 2025, reporting SG$'000 (implied by portfolio value context) with Singapore comprising 79.8% of total value and 54.3% of net lettable area. The content also includes high-level operational highlights such as a committed occupancy of 96.7%, WALE metrics, sustainability certifications, and acquisition details but contains no audited portfolio statements, profit/loss tables, gross revenue notes, tenant mix data, or distribution figures.

This page presents the **Occupancy by Committed NLA (%)** table and chart for Keppel REIT's portfolio as at 31 December 2025, detailing regional averages and specific property occupancy rates across Singapore, Australia, South Korea, and Japan. It also includes a **Geographical Breakdown of Expiring and Rent Review Leases (%)** table projecting lease activity from 2026 to 2031 based on committed attributable gross rent and NLA, alongside narrative data on Weighted Average Lease Expiry (WALE) and leasehold/freehold composition in square feet.

This page presents the Top-N tenants table and tenant mix analysis for Keppel REIT's property portfolio as of 31 December 2025, detailing the top 10 tenants by committed monthly gross rent (29.5% contribution) alongside business sector breakdowns by both gross rent and net lettable area (NLA).

This page presents the "Property Portfolio At a Glance" for Singapore, detailing four core assets (Ocean Financial Centre, Marina Bay Financial Centre, One Raffles Quay, and Keppel Bay Tower) with their locations, ownership interests, purchase prices, valuations, capitalisation rates, committed occupancy levels, FY 2025 attributable net property income, tenant counts, principal tenants, and carpark lot numbers reported in SGD'000.

This page presents an Australia Property Portfolio table detailing five specific assets, including their locations, ownership interests, purchase and valuation prices in SGD'000 and AUD'000, capitalisation rates, attributable Net Lettable Area (NLA), committed occupancy levels, FY 2025 Attributable Net Property Income (NPI), tenant counts, principal tenants, and carpark lot numbers. The data explicitly lists key financial metrics such as S$318.5 million to S$337.6 million valuations and NPI figures ranging from S$0.7 million to S$21.1 million for the reporting year ending 31 December 2025.

This page displays a table detailing the acquisition details, ownership interests, and financial highlights for five specific properties across Australia, South Korea, and Japan. The reporting unit is SGD'000 (S$), with additional foreign currency values provided for non-Australian assets, alongside key metrics such as purchase price, valuation, capitalisation rates, attributable net property income, and principal tenant information.

This page details the Ocean Financial Centre property portfolio in Singapore, featuring a tenant business sector analysis and top-five tenants table based on committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025. The content includes lease expiry profiles by year alongside descriptions of the building's features, certifications, and retail component, with all financial data presented as percentages without explicit currency or unit labels.

This page presents the Marina Bay Financial Centre, an integrated development of three Grade A office towers and a mall, featuring a donut chart table detailing tenant business sector analysis by committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025 and a subsequent table listing the top five tenants ranked by their share of total committed monthly gross rent.

This page details the property portfolio and asset specifics for One Raffles Quay, including its 1.3 million sf Grade A office space in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and BCA Green Mark Platinum certification, alongside a tenant business sector analysis by committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025. The section also presents a Top-N tenants table listing TikTok, Deutsche Bank, Ernst & Young, L'Oreal Singapore, and Capital International by their respective percentages of total committed monthly gross rent, along with a lease expiry profile categorized by year.

This page details the Keppel Bay Tower, a Grade A commercial property with 386,000 sf of space located in Singapore's HarbourFront area, featuring a tenant business sector analysis and top five tenants by committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025. The reporting unit is not explicitly stated in the text; however, the data presented includes percentages for the tenant mix, lease expiry profile, and specific tenant contributions to total committed monthly gross rent.

This page presents a property profile for 255 George Street in Sydney, featuring an audited portfolio statement of its physical attributes and a tenant business sector analysis table showing Banking, insurance and financial services at 47.6% and Government agency at 35.9% of committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025. The document also includes a top-five tenants table listing the Australian Taxation Office as the largest contributor at 35.9%, followed by Bank of Queensland at 20.8%, and a lease expiry profile indicating that 59.1% of committed rent is due from 2031 and beyond, with no financial highlights or management fee data present.

This page presents the 8 Chifley Square property profile and key tenant metrics as of 31 December 2025, featuring a Tenant Business Sector Analysis by Committed Monthly Gross Rent (%) table showing Government agencies (51.3%) as the largest sector, followed by a Top Five Tenants table listing The Reserve Bank of Australia (51.3%) and Eltav Investments (16.7%), and a Lease Expiry Profile table detailing committed rent distribution across years up to 2031 & beyond. All financial percentages are reported without explicit unit labels other than (%).

This page details the property portfolio and lease profile for 2 Blue Street in Australia, reporting figures as percentages of total committed monthly gross rent rather than in SGD'000. The main artifacts include a Tenant Business Sector Analysis showing TMT tenants contribute 62.3% of rent, a Top Five Tenants table listing Equifax (37.0%), Pacific National (24.3%), BBC Studios Australia (13.3%), Alstom Transport (12.1%), and Temenos (9.0%), and a Lease Expiry Profile indicating 52.4% of commitments expire by 2030 with no data provided for 2026–2028.

This page presents a property profile and asset-level analytics for Pinnacle Office Park, featuring a Tenant Business Sector Analysis table and a Top-N Tenants table as at 31 December 2025. The content details the building's specifications, energy ratings, and lease expiry profile by committed monthly gross rent percentages, but contains no audited portfolio statements, financial statements, or distribution highlights.

The page features a **Statement of Portfolio (property valuations)** for the Top Ryde City Shopping Centre, detailing its location, size (837,000 sf retail space), and trade area characteristics within Sydney. It includes a **Top-N tenants/customers table** listing the top five tenants by committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025, along with a lease expiry profile and tenant business sector analysis reported in percentages without specific currency units.

This page features a photograph of the 8 Exhibition Street building and presents a **TENANT BUSINESS SECTOR ANALYSIS BY COMMITTED MONTHLY GROSS RENT (%)** table showing seven sectors ranging from Banking (34.7%) to Services (0.6%). It also includes a **TOP FIVE TENANTS** table listing Ernst & Young (25.0%), UBS AG (14.5%), Kingside (8.1%), CBRE (7.8%), and Minister for Finance – State of Victoria (7.6%), alongside a lease expiry profile by committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025.

This page presents the Victoria Police Centre, a 40-storey Grade A office tower in Melbourne's CBD fully leased to the Minister for Finance – State of Victoria as shown in the Top Five Tenants table (100.0% committed monthly gross rent) and Tenant Business Sector Analysis (100.0% Government agency). The property details include its GBCA 6 Star Green Star ratings, Carbon Neutral certification, and a lease expiry profile indicating 100.0% of committed rent remains beyond 2031, with no specific financial metrics or reporting unit schema present.

This page features a main tenant business sector analysis donut chart and table showing Government agencies comprise 99.3% of the David Malcolm Justice Centre's committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025, followed by Top Five Tenants where Minister for Works – Government of Western Australia accounts for 99.3%.

This page details the South Korea portfolio of T Tower, a 28-storey Grade A building in Seoul's CBD, and presents a **Tenant Business Sector Analysis by Committed Monthly Gross Rent (%)** showing Manufacturing and distribution as the largest sector at 35.6%. The reporting unit is not explicitly stated for these percentages, but the data includes a **Top-N Tenants table** listing five major tenants with their rent contributions, a **Trade/Tenant Mix** breakdown by sector, and a **Lease Expiry Profile** indicating that 28.7% of committed rent expires in 2027.

This page presents the Property Portfolio Japan for KR Ginza II, featuring a table detailing the tenant business sector analysis by committed monthly gross rent as at 31 December 2025 and another showing the top five tenants by the same metric. The reporting unit is not explicitly stated in the provided text segments.

This page presents a DISTRIBUTABLE INCOME BY HALF YEAR table (in SGD'000) alongside narrative details on Keppel REIT's distribution of $212.4 million for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, portfolio acquisitions including Top Ryde City Shopping Centre and an additional interest in Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 3, and sustainability-focused funding metrics.

This page presents the Financial Review for Keppel REIT, featuring a comprehensive table of financial highlights reporting 2025 results in SGD'000 that details property income, net property income, share of associates, management fees, borrowing costs, fair-value changes, and profit after tax attributable to unitholders, perpetual securities holders, and non-controlling interests. The text further explains the composition of Net Property Income (NPI) from specific property interests and joint ventures, alongside key operational updates and distribution dates for the financial year ended 31 December 2025.

This page presents the **Attributable NPI by Property (%)** table and a **Statement of Portfolio (property valuations)** table for Keppel REIT, reporting values in SGD million. The portfolio valuation as at 31 December 2025 totaled $11,657.0 million, while attributable Net Property Income (NPI) for 2025 was $381.4 million, with property-specific contributions ranging from Ocean Financial Centre Interest at 19.9% to Marina Bay Financial Centre Interest at 29.4%.

This page presents a Debt Maturity Profile table showing the aggregate leverage of 47.9% and total gross borrowings of S$3,761.7 million as at 31 December 2025, alongside text detailing funding sources, interest costs, and currency hedging strategies for Keppel REIT's assets.

The page presents a **KEY STATISTICS** table detailing Keppel REIT's aggregate leverage (47.9%), interest coverage ratio (2.6 times), and weighted average cost of debt (3.41% p.a.) for the year ended 31 December 2025, alongside cash flow data from operating, investing, and financing activities reported in SGD million. It further includes a sensitivity analysis table quantifying the impact of interest rate fluctuations and AUD exchange rate changes on profit before tax in SGD'000.

This page presents the ESG Targets and Commitments table, which outlines Keppel REIT's short-term (2026), medium-term (2030), and long-term goals across Environmental Stewardship categories including Climate Action and Energy Management, Water Management, and Waste Management. The table details specific targets such as a 50% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 and reports FY 2025 performance metrics showing a 49.2% decrease in emissions and 28.2% portfolio renewable energy usage, with references to pages 86–94 for further data.

This page outlines Keppel REIT's risk management approach under its ERM Framework, specifically detailing climate-related risks assessed using ClimSystems' Climate Insights external data and internal asset characteristics against IPCC Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) 5-8.5, 2-4.5, and 1-2.6, with no audited Portfolio Statement, financial highlights, or tenant tables present.

The page presents the **Scope 1 and 2 Emissions and Intensity** table reporting Keppel REIT's direct emissions (natural gas, refrigerants, diesel) and market-based indirect emissions from electricity in tonnes of CO2e for years 2019 through 2025, alongside a corresponding GHG intensity metric expressed in tCO2e/m². A subsequent table details Scope 3 emissions across eight categories including purchased goods, capital goods, fuel activities, transportation, waste, travel, and downstream leased assets, with totals provided for 2023, 2024, and 2025 in SGD'000 equivalent units where applicable to the data structure.

This page presents a qualitative physical risk assessment table detailing Keppel REIT's identified climate-related risks (Extreme precipitation, Extreme water level, Mean sea level rise, Extreme temperature, and Heat wave days) across short-term, medium-term, and long-term horizons along with their business impacts and management responses. The reporting unit is SGD'000 as referenced in the cross-reference to the Financial Statements on page 170.

This page presents the Keppel REIT Environmental Stewardship section, detailing a table of Quantitative Physical Risk Assessment Results showing Value at Risk (VaRD) ranging from S$17 million to S$20 million for 2025 asset values and outlining qualitative transition risks regarding increasing carbon prices with corresponding business responses. The reporting unit is S$ million.

This page details Keppel REIT's water and waste management performance, featuring a Water Withdrawal table showing 2023–2025 metrics (Withdrawal: 244.3 ML/253.4 ML/242.0 ML; Intensity: 0.0021/0.0022/0.0018 ML/m²) and a Waste Generated table displaying corresponding data for the same period (Waste: 1,736/2,100/2,454 tonnes; Intensity: 0.0033/0.0040/0.0046 tonne/m²). The content describes management approaches for efficiency improvements and tenant engagement but contains no financial statements or schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio valuations, profit or loss figures, gross revenue, or distribution highlights.

This page details Keppel REIT's 2024 nature and biodiversity transition planning, including a LEAP-based assessment of its 13 assets (excluding Top Ryde City Shopping Centre) that identified one asset with high biodiversity risk. The content outlines the ENCORE tool usage for evaluating dependencies, confirms low overall operational impacts due to urban location and green building certifications, and presents the Locate, Evaluate, Assess, Prepare framework without any audited financial statements, tenant data, or distribution highlights.

This page details Keppel REIT's Sustainable Finance approach, including its externally reviewed Green Financing Framework (SQS2) and performance metrics showing 67% of total borrowings were sustainability-focused as at 31 December 2025. The reporting unit is SGD'000, with a table listing green finance transactions totaling $882 million allocated to eligible categories such as Green Buildings for projects like MBFC Tower 3, Ocean Financial Centre, and One Raffles Quay.

This page presents a Human Capital section for Keppel REIT (SGD'000 not applicable to this text) containing tables on training hours per employee by gender and category, new hires and turnover rates by gender and age group, and detailed narrative text regarding human rights due diligence, supplier codes of conduct, whistleblower policies, and organizational staffing details as of 31 December 2025. No financial statements, portfolio data, or distribution highlights are present.

This page presents the GRI Content Index, mapping 23 specific sustainability reporting standards across People and Community, Employee Health and Wellbeing, and Community Development sections to their respective pages (100–106). The index includes a confidentiality note for gender remuneration ratios on page 194–197 and directs readers to pages 100–105 for detailed disclosures on human capital management, occupational health and safety, and related incidents.

This page presents an IFRS S2 Content Index table detailing Keppel REIT's industry-based guidance metrics for energy and water management, climate change adaptation, and activity data as of the reporting period. Key data points include 100% energy consumption data coverage across the portfolio with a total of 276,165 GJ consumed (71.8% grid electricity, 28.2% renewable), 242 ML of total water withdrawn (20.3% in high water stress regions), and 14 assets classified under the Office Sector per FTSE EPRA Nareit Global Real Estate Index property sector classification system.

This page indexes the SGX REIT annual report structure, listing key financial statements including the audited Portfolio Statement on page 127 and the Consolidated Statement of Profit or Loss on page 124. No specific data tables, numerical values, or reporting units are present on this index page.

This page presents the Independent Auditor's Report to the Unitholders of Keppel REIT for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, reporting on consolidated financial statements prepared in SGD'000. The primary artifact is a table detailing Key Audit Matters, which specifically addresses the valuation of investment properties (referencing Note 3) and confirms that as at 31 December 2025, the Group's carrying value of these properties was $5.6 billion, accounting for approximately 55.8% of total assets.

This page presents the **Balance Sheets** for the SGX REIT as at 31 December 2025 and 2024, reporting GROUP and TRUST figures in SGD'000. The table details non-current and current assets (including investment properties, financial assets, and cash balances) alongside corresponding liabilities and net assets, with a specific breakdown of unitholders' funds, perpetual securities, and non-controlling interests, along with units in issue and net asset value per unit.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Profit or Loss for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, reporting GROUP revenue, expenses, management fees (Trust expenses), finance costs (Borrowing costs), fair-value changes, and tax in SGD'000. The table details a Profit before tax of SGD 517,740,000 and a final Profit for the year attributable to Unitholders of SGD 443,136,000, alongside Basic and Diluted Earnings per Unit figures.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, reporting total comprehensive income of SGD'000 with a profit attributable to unitholders of SGD'000. The table details fair-value changes, foreign currency translation differences, and other comprehensive income items, along with attribution between unitholders, perpetual securities holders, and non-controlling interests, all measured in SGD'000.

This page presents the **Distribution Statement** for SGX REIT, detailing income available for distribution to Unitholders at the beginning and end of the financial year ended 31 December 2025 ($'000) alongside specific distributions made during the period. The statement explicitly names manager's management fees paid and payable in Units, trustee's fees, and capital gains distribution within Note A, while Note B breaks down total Unitholders' distribution into taxable income, tax-exempt income, and capital gains components.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement as at 31 December 2025, detailing carrying values in SGD'000 for investment properties across Singapore, Australia, South Korea, and Japan, along with associated associates and joint ventures. The table lists specific assets such as Ocean Financial Centre and Keppel Bay Tower alongside valuation notes and holdings in entities like One Raffles Quay and Marina Bay Financial Centre Towers, reporting net assets of SGD 6,006,831'000.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) as of 31 December 2025, detailing carrying values in SGD'000 for investment properties in Singapore, Australia, South Korea, Japan, and associates/joint ventures. The total valuation across all listed assets is SGD'000 11,657,085, derived from independent valuers using capitalisation, discounted cash flow, and direct comparison methods.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) for SGX REIT's investment properties as of 31 December 2024, listing assets across Singapore, Australia, South Korea, Japan, and associates/joint ventures with independent valuer details. The total portfolio valuation amounts to $9,531,621 in SGD'000, accompanied by footnotes clarifying carrying values adjusted for specific interest percentages or rental support exclusions.

This page presents the **Statements of Movements in Unitholders' Funds** for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, reporting Group movements in total units issued ($SGD'000) and unitholders' funds ($SGD'000) including foreign currency translation reserves, hedging reserves, accumulated profits, and other reserves. Key line items include profit attributable to unitholders and non-controlling interests ($492,727 SGD'000), creation of units via management fees and private placements, distributions to unitholders ($276,593 SGD'000), and net movements from perpetual securities holders and associates/joint ventures.

This page presents the **Statement of Total Return** (attributable to unitholders) for the reporting year ended 31 December 2024, detailing movements in units in issue, foreign currency translation reserve, hedging reserve, accumulated profits, and other reserves with values reported in **SGD'000**. The table records specific transactions including a distribution of SGD'216,608 to unitholders, creation of units via management fee payments, and net increases from operations totaling SGD'120,253.

This page presents the **Statements of Movements in Unitholders' Funds** for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, detailing changes in units in issue, hedging reserves, accumulated losses, and other reserves attributable to unitholders and perpetual securities holders in SGD'000. The table records operations profit of SGD 106,026'000 (unitholders) and SGD 11,308'000 (perpetual securities), alongside transactions including creation of units, distributions totaling SGD 276,593'000 (unitholders) and SGD 9,450'000 (perpetual securities), proceeds from issuance of perpetual securities of SGD 400,000'000, and net movements resulting from fair value changes on cash flow hedges.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for SGX REIT for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, reporting net cash flows provided by operating activities of $223,337 and net cash flows used in investing activities of $(1,116,329) in SGD'000.
